requiredGrammar: ALTER TABLE with a list containing one or more RENAME INDEX or RENAME KEY actions, optionally with algorithm and lock commands.
The initial complete B-tree index namespace is resolved on one absolute ordinary stock InnoDB table. Include persistent, temporary and temporary-shadow namespaces.
Native table-qualified index names follow the 5.7 grammar and must resolve to the selected owner. Later pinned grammars accept bare names.
runtimeProfile: Native parameters, SQL mode empty, lower_case_table_names=0, utf8mb4, stock InnoDB with 16 KiB pages.

construction.operands: The resolved ordered source keys, requested exact destination identifiers, unmoved physical names, checked release and effective native policy.
construction.owner: All moves must share one resolved absolute owner and table lifetime. Direct and analyzed construction are checked before publication.
construction.namespace: Every source in the original physical index namespace is consumed at most once. Unmoved keys occupy their original names. Check native-folded uniqueness both before and after renaming. The final namespace may contain a name held by another moved source in the initial state.
construction.capacity: Require at least one move and at most 64 physical names in the original and resulting namespaces. Allow exact no-op and case-only moves.
construction.names: Names consist of 1 to 64 BMP characters with no trailing space or NUL. The primary key cannot be renamed, and no move can select a destination with the reserved native-folded PRIMARY name.
construction.role: Permit a named ordinary, unique or implicitly clustered unique B-tree source. Its prior field roles, direction, visibility and generating support persist.
construction.policy: Use the last algorithm and lock. A persistent rename can be in place, including rename of an implicit clustered unique key. COPY with NONE requires a temporary table. A temporary table refuses INPLACE. A rename of an index has no native INSTANT implementation.
construction.release: 5.6 refuses the grammar and direct construction. 5.7 and later use the same typed operation for RENAME INDEX or RENAME KEY.

observations: Observe ordered parts, exact physical names, key type, uniqueness, visibility, table field metadata, rows, next generated value and the unaffected physical sibling where present.
Canonical SQL performs all moves in one ALTER TABLE. Compare both the original accepted SQL and the emitted SQL with the independent final namespace and data rule.

Detect swapped source identity through distinct ordered key parts. Observe a successful cycle, positive fresh and case-only renames, an absent or reused original source and an occupied final destination.
Observe native rejection class and whether the pre-statement transaction marker was committed.

finite.legacyAvailability: Run registered 5.6 rejection controls for analysis and direct construction.
finite.finiteOrder: Cross life, width, topology and written order for each admitted release. A cycle at width one retains its source name. Widths below 64 retain an unrelated physical name.

assurance.P01: Check source identity on the original namespace and preserve exact, checked destination names.
assurance.P02: Reject repeated or absent sources, result name conflicts, owner incoherence, reserved names, invalid capacities and unsupported release or policy.
assurance.P03: Use closed immutable value roles and native identifiers.
assurance.P04: Compose a single final namespace from initially resolved source moves and stable occupied keys.
assurance.P05: Require detached lists, final value children and audited construction.
assurance.P06: Emit one ALTER operation and compare measured metadata, transaction and data effects.
assurance.Q01: Check all owning and local rules in restricted source shape and with independent typed negatives.
assurance.Q02: Measure all fixed direct and analyzed finite identities and exact releases; include cycles, permitted qualifiers and policy.
assurance.Q03: The initial namespace has distinct owners and keys; the resulting namespace is injective under native comparison.
assurance.Q04: Observe native effects with source-sensitive catalog data and an applied mutation that changes the identity of a moved key.
assurance.Q05: Audit exact distribution, fixed generated evidence, direct and analyzed installed layout and replay.

initialFaults: Resolve a later source against the result of earlier moves.
Disallow the occupied destination of an original source that moves in the same operation.
Allow a destination that collides with an unmoved key.
Discard a move from canonical SQL or swap two destinations and detect the changed catalog.
Alias a mutable slot in the stored move or unmoved list.
trackedBeyondThisSlice: Mixed rename, removal, visibility and addition change the final namespace together and remain separate required domains.
Foreign-key-backed owners, partitioned declarations, prefix and functional indexes, and FULLTEXT and SPATIAL indexes remain separate required domains.
